description:
We are looking for creative and ambitious individuals who are passionate about technology and innovation to work together on developing a new technology project.

We welcome people with skills in programming, web development, hardware design, and software development.

Our goal is to build a collaborative team that combines creative ideas and technical skills to turn innovative ideas into reality.
summary:
VITALOOP is an intelligent, software-based astronaut health monitoring platform designed to support astronauts during long-duration space missions. It brings multiple health indicators together in one unified dashboard, including heart rate, blood pressure, oxygen levels, sleep patterns, physical activity, mental wellbeing, and radiation exposure.

The system analyzes health data using AI-assisted analytics and compares current readings with each astronaut’s personal baseline to identify unusual changes and generate clear, graded alerts. It also provides separate dashboards for astronauts and flight surgeons, helping them monitor health conditions and make informed decisions.

One of VITALOOP’s key features is its offline-first capability, allowing the platform to continue working during communication delays or temporary loss of connection with Earth, with automatic data synchronization when connectivity returns.

VITALOOP addresses the challenge of fragmented health monitoring and limited medical support during deep-space missions. By connecting multiple health signals in one platform, it aims to support early awareness, improve crew wellbeing, and contribute to safer, more sustainable human space exploration.
details:
VITALOOP is a software-based astronaut health monitoring platform designed to support crew members during long-duration space missions. It brings multiple health indicators into one unified dashboard, including heart rate, cardiovascular health, sleep patterns, physical activity, mental wellbeing, and radiation exposure. The system works by collecting health readings from compatible wearable sensors or simulated data in the current prototype. It compares each astronaut’s readings with their personal health baseline to identify unusual changes. It then generates graded, understandable alerts that explain which indicator changed and how much it differs from the astronaut’s normal range.
VITALOOP provides separate interfaces for astronauts and flight surgeons, allowing each user to access the information relevant to their role. It is also designed with an offline-first approach: data can be stored during communication interruptions and synchronized when the connection becomes available again. Our project is developed as a web application using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. We also use browser-based camera technology and MediaPipe Face Mesh in the heart-rate estimation prototype, along with simulated health data to demonstrate the monitoring system. No dedicated wearable hardware has been developed; integration with compatible wearables is a planned future feature. What makes VITALOOP creative is its combination of personal health baselines, multiple health indicators, explainable alerts, role-based access, and offline-first operation in one platform. Instead of focusing on building a new sensor, we focus on creating a smart software layer that can work with compatible monitoring devices. During development, we considered the challenges of deep-space missions, including communication delays, limited medical support, astronaut privacy, data security, individual health differences, ease of use, and alert fatigue. Our intended impact is to support earlier awareness of potential health changes, reduce the burden of health monitoring, and help astronauts and medical teams make better-informed decisions during future space missions. The current prototype uses simulated data and is intended for demonstration and decision support. It is not a certified medical device and does not provide medical diagnosis or treatment.
